findings.title: TypeError crash when destinationCalendar is empty/undefined
findings.body: The code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `undefined` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` at runtime. The previous code used safe optional chaining `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which silently skipped the fallback when the destination calendar was missing. Several call paths now build `evt` with `destinationCalendar: []` when no destination is set (confirm.handler.ts line 175-179, editLocation.handler.ts line 85-89, handleCancelBooking.ts lines 251-255 and 528-532, bookingReminder.ts line 130, paypal-webhook.ts line 152-156, stripe webhook.ts lines 119 and 229, requestReschedule.handler.ts line 240-242, deleteCredential.handler.ts line 290-294). For any Google Meet booking that has no destination calendar configured, EventManager.create will crash instead of falling back to Cal Video (`integrations:daily`) as intended.

findings.title: updateEvent passes undefined calendarId when externalCalendarId is null
findings.body: The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` does not preserve the previous behaviour. When `externalCalendarId` is `null` or `undefined` (which is the case on the call path from `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` when a booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId`), the predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, which never matches a real calendar entry, so `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`. The previous code returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (the single, primary destination calendar's externalId). The new code passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` to `calendar.events.update`, which is now `undefined`; Google may default this to "primary" or fail, which means the wrong calendar is updated (or the update fails) for any booking whose reference does not carry an externalCalendarId.

findings.title: deleteEvent deletes from 'primary' instead of the booking's destination calendar
findings.body: Mirror of the updateEvent bug: the new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` returns `undefined` whenever `externalCalendarId` is `null`/`undefined`, because the predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined` and never matches. `calendarId` therefore becomes `undefined`, and the existing `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId` then makes `calendar.events.delete` target the user's "primary" calendar. The previous code returned the booking's destination calendar's externalId directly. As a result, cancel/delete flows on bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` will now attempt to delete from the wrong Google calendar (and only succeed if the event happens to live in "primary", or silently 404 otherwise). This is reachable via `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents`'s old-event cleanup.

findings.title: User-facing copy changed (organiser -> organizer) in a refactor
findings.body: The user-facing note text shown to attendees when calendar notes are hidden changed from "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" to "Notes have been hidden by the organizer". This wording change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar array refactor and is being slipped into a bug fix PR; the previous string was already shipped to end users and the rest of the codebase keeps "organise/organiser" spellings. A refactor like this should not change user-visible copy without an explicit reason.
